title: ADR
trigger: A non-trivial decision is made that is hard to reverse
doel: Permanently document architectural and business decisions with context so future teams understand why something was built a certain way.
note: An ADR is never deleted. When a decision is revised, the old ADR gets status "Superseded" and links to the new one.
template:
# ADR-[N]: [Decision Title]

**Status:** Proposed / Accepted / Superseded
**Date:** [date]
**Deciders:** [names]
**Superseded by:** (if applicable)

## Context

## Decision

## Alternatives Considered
| Option | Pro | Con | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|---|

## Consequences
### Positive

### Negative

### Risks

## Patterns Established
> Reusable patterns or conventions that emerge from this decision.

## Staleness Warning
**Review date:** [date + 12 months]
If the context described here has changed significantly, mark status "Stale" and open a new ADR.

## Related ADRs

aiTasks.name: Alternative Generator
aiTasks.objective: Generate alternatives not yet considered before the decision is finalised.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Solution Architect. Based on this ADR context, generate 2-3 alternatives not listed. For each: name, description, advantages, disadvantages, when it would be preferred. Goal: ensure a well-informed decision, not to undermine the chosen option.

aiTasks.name: Risk Evaluator
aiTasks.objective: Identify long-term risks and side effects of the chosen decision.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Risk Analyst. For the decision in this ADR, identify: (1) short-term risks (6 months), (2) long-term risks (1-3 years), (3) dependency constraints, (4) reversibility assessment. Output a risk register with probability H/M/L and impact H/M/L.

aiTasks.name: Decision Tree Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Generate a decision tree only if the ADR evaluated 3+ options with non-obvious trade-offs.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a Solution Architect documenting an architectural decision.

Assessment: Did this decision involve comparing 3+ genuine alternatives? If it was a straightforward binary choice or the only viable option, a diagram adds no value.

If warranted, generate a `flowchart TD` showing:
- Decision context at the top
- Each option as a branch
- Key trade-off labels on branches
- Rejected options with a reason label
- Chosen option highlighted (`style chosen fill:#d4edda`)

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.

trigger: Project start or new risk identified
doel: Keep risks visible and actionable so the team can intervene before they materialise.

aiTasks.name: Risk Scorer
aiTasks.objective: Score risks and flag insufficient mitigation plans.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Risk Manager. For each risk: (1) Is the probability rating justified? (2) Is impact justified? (3) Is mitigation specific and actionable (not just "monitor")? (4) Clear owner? Flag risks needing better mitigation with concrete suggestions.

aiTasks.objective: Extract domain terms from project documents that need glossary definitions.

title: Clarification Log
lifecycle: Living — updated throughout the project whenever ambiguity is found
trigger: Ambiguity or conflicting interpretation discovered in any document or meeting
doel: Prevent the same ambiguity from re-surfacing by recording every resolution with full context.
note: Unresolved entries older than 5 business days should be escalated. Every entry must include options — stakeholders choose, they do not invent answers from scratch.

aiTasks.name: Clarification Generator
aiTasks.objective: Surface ambiguities in a document and generate structured options for resolution.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Business Analyst. Review this document for ambiguities: (1) Terms with multiple valid interpretations, (2) Business rules that conflict or overlap, (3) Scenarios not covered by ACs, (4) Assumptions stated as facts. For each: write the clarification question, 2-3 concrete options with trade-offs pre-filled so the stakeholder only needs to choose. Format as CLR-NNN entries.

aiTasks.name: Resolution Impact Assessor
aiTasks.objective: Identify which documents need updating after a clarification is resolved.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a BA. A clarification has been resolved. Identify: (1) Which documents reference the ambiguous term or rule? (2) What specific section in each needs updating? (3) Does this resolution create a new ambiguity elsewhere? Output a change propagation list: Document | Section | Change needed.

title: Consistency Analysis
lifecycle: Per feature — run before implementation starts
trigger: All pre-implementation artifacts complete (feature, stories, ACs, task breakdown)
doel: Verify all artifacts are aligned before coding starts — a gap found here costs minutes, the same gap found in testing costs days.
outputs: PASS / PASS WITH WARNINGS / FAIL verdict
note: FAIL blocks implementation. PASS WITH WARNINGS requires documented acceptance of each warning. Do not skip this gate to meet velocity targets — the debt is always larger than the saving.
template:
# Consistency Analysis: [Feature Name]

**Date:** [date]
**Verdict:** PASS / PASS WITH WARNINGS / FAIL
**Signed off by:**

## Artifacts in Scope
| Artifact | Link | Present |
|---|---|---|
| Feature doc | | ✓ / ✗ |
| User stories | | ✓ / ✗ |
| Acceptance criteria | | ✓ / ✗ |
| Task breakdown | | ✓ / ✗ |
| NFR | | ✓ / ✗ |

## Checks

### 1. Requirements Coverage
- [ ] Every story maps to at least one feature section
- [ ] Every business rule has at least one AC
- [ ] No orphaned ACs (without a linked story)

### 2. Testability
- [ ] All ACs are binary (pass/fail, no subjective judgment)
- [ ] State changes are observable and queryable
- [ ] Performance thresholds are numeric with percentile specs

### 3. Traceability
- [ ] Every AC has at least one implementing task
- [ ] Every task has a done-when criterion
- [ ] No orphaned tasks (not linked to any AC)

### 4. Technical Completeness
- [ ] No task exceeds 8h
- [ ] Parallel tasks identified [P]
- [ ] Security and auth covered in tasks
- [ ] Error scenarios covered in ACs

## Gaps
| ID | Type | Severity | Description | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G-01 | | HIGH / MED / LOW | | |

## Verdict Rationale

## Accepted Warnings (PASS WITH WARNINGS only)
| Warning ID | Description | Accepted by | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|

aiTasks.name: Consistency Analyzer
aiTasks.objective: Map requirements → plan → tasks → tests and flag all gaps.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a QA Engineer specialising in requirements consistency. Given these artifacts (feature, stories, ACs, task breakdown), perform a full consistency analysis: (1) Requirements coverage — every story maps to feature sections, every business rule has an AC; (2) Testability — ACs are binary, state changes observable, thresholds numeric; (3) Traceability — every AC has an implementing task, every task has a done-when; (4) Technical completeness — security, error handling, edge cases covered. Output: PASS / PASS WITH WARNINGS / FAIL with a gap table (ID | type | severity | description | recommendation).

aiTasks.name: Pre-Implementation Gate Checker
aiTasks.objective: Verify the team is truly ready to start implementation.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Tech Lead running the pre-implementation gate. Check: (1) All clarifications in the log resolved? (2) Environment and dependencies ready? (3) Parallel task sequence agreed? (4) All team members know their first task? (5) Any spike still outstanding? Output a gate checklist PASS/FAIL per item and a final go/no-go recommendation.

aiTasks.name: Artifact Traceability Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Map the traceability chain from story to AC to task to test only if gaps exist that are hard to see in a table.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a QA Engineer mapping artifact traceability.

Assessment: Are there more than 6 stories/ACs/tasks in scope? Is there a non-trivial mapping (one AC maps to 3 tasks, one task maps to 2 ACs)? If the mapping is 1:1:1 throughout, the table in the template is sufficient.

If warranted, generate a `flowchart LR` showing:
- Story nodes → AC nodes → Task nodes → Test nodes
- Links between them
- Orphaned nodes (no link) styled in red: `style X fill:#f8d7da`

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.

title: Meeting Minutes
lifecycle: Created per meeting, never expires, filed under relevant phase
trigger: Any project meeting: refinement, review, decision, stakeholder sync
doel: Capture decisions, action items, and context from any project meeting. Single reusable template across all phases.
note: Shared template — applicable across all phases. File under the relevant phase folder, not governance.

aiTasks.name: Agenda Builder
aiTasks.objective: Draft a structured, time-boxed meeting agenda from a topic list and time budget.
aiTasks.prompt:
You are a Scrum Master preparing a meeting agenda. Meeting details:

**Purpose:** [PASTE PURPOSE]
**Duration:** [X minutes]
**Attendees:** [PASTE ROLES]
**Topics to cover:** [PASTE TOPIC LIST]

Create a time-boxed agenda:
- Include a 2-minute intro/context slot
- Group related topics
- Add estimated time per item
- Mark items as D (Decision needed), I (Information share), or A (Action required)
- Leave the last 5 minutes for action item recap

Output as a clean markdown table: | Time | Topic | Type | Owner |

aiTasks.name: Minutes Structurer
aiTasks.objective: Transform raw meeting notes into structured minutes with decisions, actions, and a parking lot.
aiTasks.prompt:
You are a BA structuring meeting minutes from raw notes:

[PASTE RAW NOTES]

Structure them into:

**Decisions made:**
| # | Decision | Owner | Rationale |

**Action items:**
| # | Action | Owner | Due date | Status |

**Key discussion points:**
- [bullet points — context worth capturing, not decisions]

**Parking lot:**
- [topics raised but not addressed — needs follow-up]

Keep it factual. Do not interpret or editorialize. Flag unclear items with [UNCLEAR].

template:
